title: Single anyons and anyon binding in a quantum Hall dot
authors: Marco Valentini, Will Wang, Amir Shapour Mohammadi, Noah Samuelson, Chengxuan Li, Liam Cohen, Mark Zakharyan, Jiechao Feng, Taige Wang, Takashi Taniguchi, Kenji Watanabe, Michael P. Zaletel, Andrea F. Young
abstract: Anyons are particles with quantized fractional statistics. In theory, a single anyon can be stabilized as a localized fractional charge within the bulk of a topologically ordered two-dimensional insulator. However, experiments to date have focused on probing anyons in structures in which many anyonic excitations coexist and interact. Here, we demonstrate the trapping of a single anyon in a device consisting of a graphene-based quantum point contact with an embedded tunable quantum Hall dot. Benchmarking our device at v = 1, we demonstrate backscattering between Fermi liquid edge states mediated by the whole-electron Coulomb blockade of the dot. The cleanliness and control available in our device allow depletion of the dot to the last quasihole, and we observe spin blockade for transitions to the opposite-spin Landau level. At v = 1/3 and 2/3, we observe backscattering resonances with three times the frequency, consistent with resonant transmission of e/3 charges via a single anyon transistor. We demonstrate controlled depletion to the last quasiparticle to form a single anyon quantum dot. Tracing the charge addition spectrum for quasiparticle number Nqp = 1-5, we observe highly irregular addition energies, consistent with DMRG modeling showing a complex orbital shell-filling behavior. At higher Nqp = 10-20, the addition energies show a striking pattern: quasiholes at 1/3 (and quasiparticles at 2/3) show a regular addition spectrum while quasiparticles at 1/3 (and quasiholes at 2/3) do not. We trace the origin of this irregularity to an attractive component of the inter-anyon interaction: by experimentally tuning the confining energy, we observe complete suppression of alternating charge sectors, after which the dot charges in increments of twice the fundamental charge. This observation indicates the emergence of an anyon binding energy as large as the charging energy.
summary: This work reports on the experimental realization and characterization of a single anyon quantum dot using a graphene-based quantum Hall structure. By measuring the charge addition spectrum, the researchers observed signatures of an attractive inter-anyon interaction, leading to the quantitative evidence of an anyon binding energy. This advances the field by moving from ensemble measurements to single-particle characterization of fractional excitations.
main_problem: The research aims to experimentally demonstrate the trapping of a single anyon and characterize the associated anyon binding energy in a controlled quantum Hall dot setup.
main_result: The authors observed highly irregular charge addition energies at low quasiparticle numbers, which transitioned to a regular pattern indicating an anyon binding energy comparable to the charging energy.
method: The study uses charge spectroscopy by measuring the addition energy spectrum of quasiparticles/quasiholes across a graphene-based quantum point contact coupled to a tunable quantum Hall dot.
model_or_system: The physical system is a graphene-based quantum point contact coupled to a tunable quantum Hall dot, allowing the study of fractional excitations (anyons) in a topologically ordered insulator.
key_observables: Charge addition spectrum, conductance plateaus at fractional fillings (e.g., 1/3, 2/3), and the spacing ($\delta$) of Coulomb blockade resonances.
important_parameters:
Fractional filling factors ($
u=1/3, 2/3$), charging energy ($E_C$), and the ratio of inter-anyon interaction to charging energy.
main_assumptions: The system is modeled as containing a single localized anyon, and the analysis relies on interpreting conductance dips as single-anyon tunneling events.
figures_summary: Figures detail device schematics, quantized conductance plateaus at integer and fractional fillings, and plots showing the spacing of Coulomb resonances ($\delta$) as a function of gate voltages.
paper_structure:
The paper progresses from demonstrating basic fractional charge transport ($
u=1/3$) to observing complex, non-monotonic addition energy spectra, culminating in the identification of an energy scale suggesting anyon binding.
why_interesting: The direct experimental observation of anyon binding energy in a solid-state platform provides crucial empirical data for theoretical models of fractional quantum Hall states and topological matter.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Integer and fractional quantum Hall quantum dot. a, Device schematic. A monolayer graphene layer is encapsulated between hexagonal boron nitride dielectrics (not shown) and controlled by 7 field-effect gates in three vertical layers. A graphite bottom gate (at voltage VB) tunes the entire device. A top graphite gate (VT) is patterned using atomic force lithography[17] to form a QPC geometry consisting of a central top gate perforated by a hole of 90 nm diameter as well as north and south QPC control gates (Vqpc,N and Vqpc,S) (see atomic force micrograph, inset). Three aluminum finger gates are aligned over the hole (Vdot) and trenches (Vedge,N and Vedge,S) close to the dot....

Single quasihole-quasiparticle control in the integer regime. a, I/V as a function of VDC and Vdot under the same conditions as in Fig. 1g, but with Vedge = −3.5 V. b, Low-bias data acquired under the same conditions as in a. c, Schematic of the dot embedded in the QPC for Nqp < 0 and d, Nqp > 0. The left panels show a real-space diagram while the right panels show the energy as a function of y-coordinate across the QPC neck. Edge-to-dot tunneling is allowed for Nqp < 0 but spin-blockaded for Nqp > 0. e, High-bias data acquired under the same conditions as panel a for Nqp > 0. f, Schematic of the dot embedded in the QPC for Nqp > 0 and applied bias exceeding the Zeeman energy....

Panels a and d correspond to the quasihole regime, whereas b and c correspond to the quasiparticle regime.
